# Auto-generated rule: console.log + process.exit() drops stdout above the pipe buffer — on an exit-0 protocol that means fail-open

Node stdout is ASYNC on a pipe (macOS). Anything past the 64 KiB kernel pipe buffer sits in the libuv write queue and process.exit() discards it. Harmless while the exit CODE carried the decision; fatal once the decision moved into stdout JSON with exit 0 — a truncated envelope reads as no-decision and the tool call is ALLOWED. Fix is two-part: clamp the payload to a budget derived from the real worst case, AND write synchronously via fs.writeSync(1) with an EAGAIN retry loop. Clamp alone does not protect a caller that bypasses it; sync write alone ships 200 KB envelopes.

## Evidence
2026-07-29 emitDeny: reasonLen 70000 -> stdoutBytes 65536, parses=false, decision=NONE (before); parses=true, decision=deny (after). Directly reachable via pre-bash-templates-first, which puts the whole unbounded Bash command in the reason. The SAME defect independently surfaced in check-test-value-bans.mjs --json piped into jq (135576 bytes truncated at ~64 KiB).
